evidence:
Verdict basis (frozen task .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r6/task, input sha cefa38a9...; solution/ and environment/assets/seed_data.json are byte-identical to the workspace project per diff -rq).
1) Committed static baseline, not regenerated or fetched: solution/solve.sh only verifies no process holds DB_PATH, then `cp -a "$(dirname "$0")/app/." /app/` and `rm -f` of the disposable app.db/-wal/-shm. No npm install, no build step, no download; package.json pins better-sqlite3 12.4.1 and express 5.1.0, matching the globals installed at exact versions in environment/Dockerfile. index.html loads only /styles.css and /js/{board,threads,app}.js (no CDN); the server makes no outbound request; the only client fetch is to same-origin API paths (public/js/app.js:29). Compared with the template solve.sh (plain cp -a), the task adds only a guarded DB reset, which makes each install start from the same fresh seed.
2) Deterministic seeding: solution/app/src/seed_data.json equals environment/assets/seed_data.json (both sha256 a1c65c80...). db.js seedIfEmpty runs only when users is empty, in one transaction, inserting seed ids verbatim. Seeded applications get the constant created_at '2026-06-15T09:00:00Z' (src/db.js:75), and seeded messages and notes keep their seed created_at. Message ids come from AUTOINCREMENT in file order. Each conversation's seed timestamps strictly increase and are unique (APP-101 120, APP-201 3, APP-301 3, APP-302 1), so file order and time order agree, and read markers (read_count -> ids[app][n-1]) resolve the same way on every run. Seeded positions are unique within every job/stage. The graded seeded facts (functional prompt Z: Platform Engineer Applied order Greta Lindqvist, Ade Bello, Marco Rossi; Screen order Priya Nair, Samuel Ortiz; Lena's unread count 1; Noor's note text) are therefore fixed by seed bytes. Every board, thread and activity query has a total ORDER BY (position,id / id).
3) Runtime nondeterminism exists but touches no pinned value. index.js:59 `now = () => new Date().toISOString()` stamps rows created at runtime, index.js:60 `uid = p => p-<3 random bytes hex>` gives ids to new jobs and applications, and index.js:88 creates session tokens. No brief or rules text defines a fixed clock or any time-dependent rule (instruction.md and hireops_rules.md contain no date/clock rule; the integration note has none). No judge.toml or prompt pins a timestamp, date or generated id. Criteria use ids only as values observed during the same run (for example the hro_candidate_no_staff replay and the C refusal 'identifier ... the app's own staff data shows'). The UI's `when()` formatting (app.js:21) is fixed to en-GB/UTC and is not graded.
4) Measured support: qc/runs/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r6/raw-evidence-index.json entries were rehashed. All six artifact hashes match, and all matching_source_files hashes match the frozen bytes. results/workspace.json (kind 'Scripted golden observations; not a configured judge run') reports 22 groups, with page_errors [] and passed=true for 'seeded card order and internal notes are loaded', 'unread counts per person...' and 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages and activity without reseeding'. This is one scripted golden run, not a repeat-run determinism measurement, and not a configured judge, Oracle or model score.
Adversarial probes: (a) Broken reference that could pass: a solve.sh that ran npm install from the registry or fetched seed at boot. Not present. (b) Conforming alternative that could fail: an implementation that sorts seeded messages by created_at instead of file order, or one that uses UUIDs and real timestamps. Neither changes graded values, because per-thread order is unambiguous and no criterion pins ids or times. Latent P3 observation only: the candidate list is ordered by created_at,id, and runtime-created apps use a wall-clock time and a random id. Two applications for one candidate created in the same millisecond could order randomly. Ordering of the candidate list is not graded, and the seeded rows share a constant timestamp but are tie-broken by fixed ids. Residual: repeat-run reproducibility was inferred from source and one scripted run, not measured across multiple fresh installs; the full configured judge run is absent (relevant to other rows, not a defect here).
